item.content:encoded:
What do you mean 'cultural insensitivity'? This article didn't mangle the legend or stereotype Japanese culture or have racist writings or do anything that's actually culturally insensitive. What's wrong with writing about a popular Japanese myth? If anything, the authors are helping expand people's horizons by introducing them to the wonderful weirdness in Japanese mythology.

Seriously, when writing about Japan, don't just write about 妖怪, let alone popular or recognizable ones such as kappa or gashadokuro. I'm still waiting on an SCP about Futakichi-onna, the woman with two mouths; Nurikabe, a spirit acting as a wall misdirecting travelers at night; or Ashiarai Yashiki, a…giant foot that smashes through roofs and demands a washing.

Then start writing them yourself instead of complaining that there aren't any.

item.content:encoded:
Sure. To begin with, gathered some reference for Shushu-In and related groups in the JP articles and forum posts. (note: Shushu-In has many more articles other than these, mostly just with the description like 'once Shushu-In had this, later the Foundation succeeded to.')

domestic survey report
– hide block

http://ja.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-2035180
A thread of Shushu-In posted in Dec 2016 with links to past similar threads. While there's no concerted predecessor, some users shared an interesting idea about Sen no Rikyu? being the mastermind of the earliest period Shushu-In.

http://ja.scp-wiki.net/kwana-1
http://ja.scp-wiki.net/hal-aki-s-proposal
Shushu-In as an organization that is alternative of the Foundation in a magic-based world.

http://ja.scp-wiki.net/collected-item-no19316
Shushu-In containing the Foundation by a magical mean.

http://ja.scp-wiki.net/hirose-tale02
Shushu-In, presumably at an alternative universe, communicating (and getting polluted) with yet another universe. Also this document was recovered when the Foundation raided a branch of a GoI which was considered to have some relation with Shushu-In, so it's spanning three universes.

http://ja.scp-wiki.net/seafield13-1
http://ja.scp-wiki.net/kte-3317-green-sunset
http://ja.scp-wiki.net/tonannotubasa
Jushich Mikawa, an ex-IJA major and the leader of Mikawa Kikan that was the IJA's pipe with Shushu-In. Visit Europe to receive objects from Axis countries after their surrender, and went missing. Recently reappeared as a leader of an far-right group with his name. Thought as became some kind of reality-bender post-war, GOC designates him as KTE-3317 Green Sunset.

http://ja.scp-wiki.net/2th-goi-contest-hub10
http://ja.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-1270849
Minor GoIs partly originating from Shushu-In and born post-war.

http://ja.scp-wiki.net/goc-far-east-orientation
五行結社 (Gogyo-Kessha, Five Elements Association), originates from a faction of Onmyoryo and became member of the Council of 108. Known as extremely hostile to Unit Negative Numbers.

http://ja.scp-wiki.net/scp-1912-jp
Mentions cooperation with the Foundation in 1930 and 'marge in 1945 after collaborative relationship.' Also, there's an Esoterica Department in the Foundation.

http://ja.scp-wiki.net/scp-1200-jp
In the last days of the war, Shushu-In cooperated with The Supreme War Council to protect Kyoto from war damage, as 70% of Mainland objects they collected was contained there. This effort ended up exploiting a reality-bending entity to transfer a nuclear bomb to an extradimensional realm, eventually neutralizing the entity.

http://ja.scp-wiki.net/seafield13-tale-2-2
An obscure staff is being asked to translate 'Secure, Contain, Protect' to Japanese. Mentions the upper echelons ignoring approaches from the Foundation before the surrender.

Other recurrent and/or fragmented settings:

  • Other than 研儀官 (higikan, mystagogue; a researcher without any meaningful thaumaturgic power, or a staff who does paperwork or bureaucratic tasks) and 秘儀官 (higikan, mystic), there are several kin groups specialized as physical assault force(s) or espionage unit(s) doing such jobs as traditional family businesses, usually called 刀 (katana).
  • Some ex-Shushu-In members with anomalous properties, possibly stemming from the UNN 'super soldier' project and many of them have anomalies of de facto immortality or rejuvenation, are employed by the Foundation.
  • Recently a KO user made inquiry at the JP forum about the idea of North Korea GoI which has had recovered anomalies UNN had left in the Korean Peninsula when they had gone back to Mainland Japan after the war. The answer was that Ashifune has surrendered almost every remaining anomaly he gathered for UNN to the Foundation.

And there are some more minor GoIs from the alternative universe(s) and possibly have something to do with the Axis powers too.

http://ja.scp-wiki.net/sadahiko-s-homepage-html
http://ja.scp-wiki.net/system:page-tags/tag/%E8%89%A6%E9%9A%8A#pages

艦隊 (Kantai, the Fleet) consists of ships from various ages/backgrounds, perhaps including IJN. 幻島同盟 (The Confederate Island Countries of Phantom) consists of phantom islands and legendary lands. It sees Kantai as a hostile group, and refers to Thule as an ever-mysterious place/group.

In EN, SCP-824 was initially discovered in 'an extradimensional, self-contained region accessible from a point in southern China,' and later in a small community in Japan where residents 'have not been cooperative with Foundation personnel, and generally react with suspicion to inquiries about or studies of SCP-824-1,' with records from 1937. And SCP-2928 made my headcanon that Shushu-In was skillful at anti-memetics.

As for Shushu-in, how were they during World War II? Forced to assist Japan? Neutral?

In the case of SCP-1200-JP, it seems to me that it's implying Shushu-In was reluctant about other form of collaboration. If Kyoto had been blown up, there would have been XK-senario in that plot. So cooperation may be for the sake of protection of normalcy, not (only) for the Empire. It also seems like, for some reason, they couldn't take proactive means to fend off attacks rather than waiting for the airplanes to come. Apart from this, Shushu-In being relatively free from the Imperial Japanese government seems rather popular as a headcanon.

P.S. Piercing together those information, I think here we got some neat idea to get a few things work well. For example, how to survive in a post-war world in the form of paramilitary groups such as IJAMEA:

  • Utilizing anomalous spaces, just like Yokai Yokocho, as shelters and/or secret HQs.
  • Hiding in remote and low-level population areas, as of SCP-824-1.
  • Hiding entrances for hideouts, hideouts themselves, or personnel with anti-memetic technology.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
IJAMEA, like all apparatus of Imperial Japan, should have died down after the war. It normally won't have such influence into the 21st century (to the point of a base in China, of all things), and yet they do. It brings into question as to how active they still are in the modern era, that not even Japan's defeat in WWII has stopped their drive.

I've been working on a draft that was for the history contest but apparently late. This is centered around an anomalous community in modern Japan, but also mentions IJAMEA in its pre-history. In it I tried (and am trying) to justify co-existence of IJAMEA, Shūshū-In (JP GoI, an anomalous agency of Imperial Japan) and Yōkai batallion.

FYI, many of JP member (30% in this survey) think Shūshū-In, IJAMEA, Onmyōryō and Unit Negative Numbers (an anomalous IJA agency superficially dedicated to study anomalous war technology) can co-exist in a same timeline.1 Collision happening here is that Shūshū-In would be dismantled in 1945, and most of surviving personnel were hired by the Foundation or GOC, amnesticized to send back to general population or terminated. Few dissidents managed to evade those fates and formed often-namesake groups, many of them hostile.

SPOILER!!!
– hide block

It's basically about ambition and finesse of Ashifune. He utilized IJA to gain power in Shūshū-In. Unit Negative Numbers' purpose was to create super soldiers, but it was actually for his pursuit of immortality. At the latest in the 1944, he betrayed his country and groups, approached to the Foundation, and make a bargain to be acquitted of his past seizure of objects and assume some good position in the Foundation after collapse of the Imperial-military regime. Eventually assassinated on August 16, 1945, he was reincarnated as Agent Kanahebi, and later became the Director of Site-9█.

Mostly from Agent Kanahebi's personal file (Japanese) since Unit Negative Numbers has barely GoI-worthy number of articles, and Shūshū-In's mainly focused to contemporary 'dissidents' activities, with only fragmented past information. It's also worth noting that the Ashifune-Kanahebi identity plot is not obviously written.

I'm not so inclined to perfectly unify the canon around this, though. I just hope this will give some more depth and new perspective.

Footnotes
1. 29% say they have some special relation inter-universe, 23% answered they don't know enough about these groups, and 18% deny co-existence.

item.content:encoded:
Wow, a GoI format for IJAMEA! At last.

But then, for my Japanese-native eyes the typeface of the logo is too arid, and a bit feels like anachronism.

And in Japan, it's hard to convince people you're doing cool things if they have MS gothic from hell in their visual design.

Imperial Japanese military organizations generally don't have insignias like Western counterparts outside flags, so a text logo is not a poor choice, but since brush calligraphy is widely used in such cases, it would be far better and realistic, and looks serious if it is done with gorgeous, glorious brush-written style.
ex. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Japanese_calligraphy_logos https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RITSUMEIKAN_Wooden_Plaque_by_Prince_Saionji_(Kyoto,_Japan).JPG

Or, use seal script, mainly small seal script. As to looking formal and governmental, it may be the best choice. It's usually used for seals as its name says, but many military decorations also adopted this style, and the Japanese passport of today uses it too.
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:1931-34_China_Incident_War_Medal-003.JPG
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:1904-1905_Russo-Japanese_War_medal_reverse.jpg
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:1931-34_China_Incident_War_Medal-002.JPG
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:JapanpassportNew10y.PNG
with clerical script: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Victory_medal_Japan_(revers)_crop.jpg
seal-ish script: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:1939_Border_War_Medal_04.JPG https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Air_attack_of_Philippines_medal.jpg

Plus, I prefer only 異 rather than putting both 異 and 常. It may be because somehow my browser is making the red circle look vertically stretched, however, and would possibly not look so terrible if it's a true circle. Of course this is just my aesthetic preference, so other Japanese speakers may have different opinions.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Like I said during a critique, this feels quite interesting for one reason. IJAMEA, like all apparatus of Imperial Japan, should have died down after the war. It normally won't have such influence into the 21st century (to the point of a base in China, of all things), and yet they do. It brings into question as to how active they still are in the modern era, that not even Japan's defeat in WWII has stopped their drive.

While unaddressed here, it begs to ask what kind of methods they resorted to in order to outlast the postwar years that deliberately dismantled Japanese imperialism and raised a generation of militarism-adverse Japanese?

Overall, this helps to give IJAMEA some shelf life outside of the Imperial Japan era.

P.S. I think I can crosslink SCP-2511 to yours. I just need to figure out the proper place.

item.content:encoded:
This is a proof-of-concept and template for a GOI-format that hopefully you'll be seeing more of soon.

The IJAMEA has become something of a passion project of mine recently, and we're working on a hub, which will be out soonish.

Everyone is free to use the CSS module for their own IJAMEA work (and encouraged to do so).

Thanks to MrWrong, Roget, and everyone else who peaked at this in chat.

EDIT: w/r/t yokai vs youkai: "youkai" is our settled upon spelling for use in the battalion, "yokai" is my preferred romanization. If this really bothers people, I will change it.

EDIT2: in case you didnt get it, this references MrWrong's SCP-2511 and my own SCP-2235
